items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: Charlie Parker’s still the GOAT man. He’s still the GOAT.

ctx.x: Yeah I mean that’s cool, but to me his association with Charlie Parker man. You know? That Bird actually mentioned him in a couple of books, like Ross Russell’s Bird Lives. When Bird actually says that the reason that he — when he visited New York with Jay McShann back in the early ‘40s, and he decided to stay in New York because he went to a jam session at Monroe’s and he heard a new form of music being played under the leadership of a pianist named Allen Tinney. And that made him want to stay in New York and…

rehearsal one day, ‘cause we used to rehearse four or five days a week. We were like on the city payroll and did concerts all the time. Somebody came in and said, “Al, your name is in this book, this Charlie Parker book and Bird’s talking about you man, talking about how great you were and how he learned from you. And the people said, “Aw, no way man.” The guy brought the book in and said, “Look. There’s your man you know.” So everybody was kind of really in awe. So somebody was saying, one of the young guys was…
